findings.title: AKS cluster without RBAC
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster with role_based_access_control_enabled = false disables Kubernetes RBAC, giving every credential full cluster access.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without network policy
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster with no network_policy in network_profile allows unrestricted pod-to-pod traffic. Enable a network policy engine (azure or calico).
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard permissions with the minimum scoped Azure RBAC roles the workload needs. Use Entra ID groups, managed identities, and Privileged Identity Management for privileged roles.

findings.title: AKS cluster without pod-managed identity
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster addon_profile without aci_connector_linux or workload identity misses pod-level identity. Prefer workload identity for pod authentication.
findings.evidence: pod_identity = absent (no pod identity or workload identity)
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster with local admin accounts enabled
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without local_account_disabled = true keeps the built-in cluster-admin Kubernetes account active, bypassing Azure AD authentication. Disable local accounts and use Azure AD / Microsoft Entra ID RBAC.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without Azure AD RBAC integration
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without an azure_active_directory_role_based_access_control block cannot map Kubernetes RBAC to Microsoft Entra ID identities, leaving cluster access to local accounts. Enable Azure AD RBAC integration.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without Key Vault secrets provider
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without a key_vault_secrets_provider block cannot mount secrets from Azure Key Vault as CSI volumes, pushing workloads toward Kubernetes Secrets or environment variables. Enable the Key Vault secrets provider addon.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in Azure Key Vault and reference them via Key Vault references or managed identities. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.title: AKS cluster without Microsoft Defender for Containers
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without a microsoft_defender block misses Defender for Containers threat detection on the cluster and its images. Enable Microsoft Defender for Containers.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without image cleaner
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without image_cleaner_enabled = true never evicts stale, potentially vulnerable container images from node caches. Enable the AKS image cleaner.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without cost analysis
findings.description: Hygiene: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without cost_analysis_enabled = true has no cost visibility into cluster spend. Enable the cost analysis addon.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without automatic upgrade channel
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without automatic_upgrade_channel defaults to no automatic upgrades, missing Kubernetes security patches. Set an upgrade channel (patch, stable, rapid, node-image). (Strict complement of AEGIS-AZURE-073, which covers an explicit "none" value.)
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without OIDC issuer
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster without oidc_issuer_enabled defaults the OIDC issuer to off, blocking workload identity federation for pod-level Azure credentials. Enable the OIDC issuer. (Strict complement of AEGIS-AZURE-076, which covers an explicit false value.)
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster without node OS auto-upgrade
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster with node_os_upgrade_channel other than "SecurityPatch" or "NodeImage" (or absent) leaves node OS patching manual, so kernel CVEs linger. Set node_os_upgrade_channel = "SecurityPatch".
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS API server exposed without authorized IP ranges
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster that is not private (private_cluster_enabled) and has no api_server_access_profile.authorized_ip_ranges exposes the Kubernetes API to the internet. Use a private cluster or restrict API access to known ranges.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: AKS cluster with run command enabled
findings.description: azurerm_kubernetes_cluster with run_command_enabled (the provider default) allows command execution on nodes via the Azure API, bypassing kubectl RBAC. Disable it unless break-glass node access is required.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
